common.name: id
common.what: The step's name, unique in its pipeline, counting the steps a Call inlines. Errors and exceptions name it.

shared.name: filter
shared.what: A condition. The step runs only on records where it is true; every other record passes unchanged. Unroll refuses one. The GUI calls it filter.

shared.name: disabled
shared.what: Skips the step, so every record passes it unchanged. The GUI's pause button sets it.

kinds.name: Parser
kinds.summary: Reads a text field as JSON, CSV, Key/value or Regex/Grok into fields.

settings.name: input
settings.what: The text field to read. Defaults to `_raw`.

settings.name: into
settings.absent: `$`, the top level of the record
settings.what: The object the parsed fields go under, such as `app`. In the GUI this is **write into**, under **Advanced**. Declared fields are named as the parse finds them, so a declared `status` lands typed at `app.status`. If `app` already holds an object, each parsed key replaces the key of its name and the others stay. If an earlier step made `app` something other than an object, the step does not compile. If a record arrives with an `app` that is not an object, the parsed object replaces it and the record gets a [`CoercionRefused`](/docs/code-reference#exceptions) exception. [`$`](/docs/code-reference#names) is the record itself, its top level.

settings.name: kind
settings.what: The format and its own settings, such as `{"type": "csv", "delimiter": ","}`. See [Formats](#formats).

values.what: Reads one line of delimited values into the declared columns. Takes `delimiter`. See [CSV](#csv).
Matches the text against patterns and keeps the named captures. Takes `patterns`. See [Regex/Grok](#grok).

settings.name: declared
settings.what: Each field's `name` and `type`. For CSV these are the columns in order; for Regex/Grok, the pattern's captures. A `datetime` field can name its format.

kinds.name: Eval
kinds.summary: Sets fields to the values of expressions.

settings.name: assignments
settings.what: Each `target` field is set to its `expr`, in order. Dots in a target name a nested field.

kinds.name: Code
kinds.summary: Runs a program on each record.

settings.name: body
settings.what: The program run on each record the step processes.

kinds.name: Drop
kinds.summary: Removes each record where a condition is true.

settings.name: condition
settings.what: Drops the record where it is true. A null condition keeps the record. The GUI's blank is `false`.

settings.name: pairs
settings.what: Each pair moves the field `from` to `to`, in order.

kinds.name: Lookup
kinds.summary: Adds fields from the rows of a lookup table that match a value.

settings.name: input
settings.what: The record's value to look up. Dots name a nested field.

settings.name: table
settings.what: The [lookup table](#lookup-tables) to match, by id.

settings.name: matchKind
settings.what: How the table is compared with the input. An MMDB table takes `cidr`.

values.what: Finds the rows whose `keyColumn` equals the input.
Finds the rows whose `keyColumn` holds a network that contains the input address.
Finds the rows whose `keyColumn` is a regular expression that matches somewhere in the input.

settings.name: multiplicity
settings.what: Which matching rows it writes the outputs from. The editor names them Most exact, First match and All matches.

values.what: Writes from the most exact matching row: the longest prefix for `cidr`, the longest pattern for `regex`, and the first matching row for `exact`.
Writes from the first matching row in table order.
Writes from every matching row, in table order, so each output is an array. An MMDB table refuses it.

settings.name: keyColumn
settings.what: The table column compared with the input. An MMDB table has none.

settings.name: outputs
settings.what: Each output writes the table's `source` column, or an MMDB record's dotted path, to the record's `field`, with an optional `type` (`str` unless given) and `default` on a miss (null unless given).

kinds.name: Unroll
kinds.summary: Turns each item of an array field into its own record.

settings.name: field
settings.what: The field that holds the array.

settings.name: keepParentFields
settings.what: Whether every new record also carries the original record's other fields.

kinds.name: Call
kinds.summary: Runs another pipeline's steps in place.

settings.name: pipeline
settings.what: The id of the pipeline whose steps run here.

kinds.name: If
kinds.summary: Sends each record through one of two lists of steps.

settings.name: condition
settings.what: A bool expression. A null condition reads false. Any other type is refused when you save.

settings.name: then
settings.what: The steps for records where the condition is true.

settings.name: else
settings.what: The steps for every other record.

kinds.name: Comment
kinds.summary: Holds a note. Records pass it unchanged.

settings.name: text
examples: Fields below come from the firewall's syslog header.
Drops load-balancer health checks before the lookup, so they cost nothing downstream.
settings.what: The note.

common.name: splitDots
common.absent: `false` for JSON and CSV, `true` for Key/value and Regex/Grok
common.what: Whether a dot in a field name nests the field.

kinds.name: CSV
kinds.summary: Reads one line of delimited values into the declared columns.

settings.name: delimiter
settings.what: The one ASCII character between values. Defaults to `,`.

settings.name: pairSep
settings.what: What separates one pair from the next. Defaults to a space.

settings.name: kvSep
settings.what: What separates a key from its value. Defaults to `=`.

settings.name: quote
settings.what: The character that quotes a value holding separators. Defaults to `"`.

settings.name: nextKey
settings.what: Whether an unquoted value runs to the `pairSep` before the next key: in `level=info debug x=1`, `level` is `info debug`. Off, `debug` is a bare key, `debug=true`.

kinds.name: Regex/Grok
kinds.summary: Matches the text against patterns and keeps the named captures.

settings.name: customPatterns
settings.what: Each `name` stands for its `pattern` in `%{NAME:field}`, beside the [built-in patterns](#grok-patterns).

settings.name: patterns
settings.what: Patterns tried in order; the first that matches gives the fields.
